newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JULY 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - BULGARIAN BUSINESS WEEKLIES-JULY 7.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Bulgarian business weeklies on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Bulgaria's tobacco monopolist, the state-owned holding Bulgatabac, has extended a licences for production of Bulgarian brands of cigarettes to six firms in Russia, Ukraine, Georgia and Moldova, its director Boiko Kishkov said. He added that under a project for restructuring of the enterprise, some 30 percent of its production should be exported abroad, mainly to Russia and CIS.

-- The cabinet lifted a $2,000 annual limit on purchase of dollars for personal use on the domestic market following introduction of a currency board, but Bulgarians still need a bank document to carry more than $1,000, when travelling abroad.

-- Bulgaria's Deputy Prime Minister and Public Works Minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev has ordered two municipalities to halt the sale of land to Bulgarian-Russian gas company Topenergy for the enlargement of a gas pipeline to Turkey, saying the sales did not meet legal requirements.
-- Bulgaria has planted only 4,300 ha with sugar beet this year, down from 17,500 ha five years ago and 40,400 ha in 1989.

-- The executive director of Bulgaria's gas monopolist Bulgargas Petar Sabev has submitted his resignation. Sabev was critisised for a flawed gas supplies contract with Topenergy joint gas company which he signed last year under pressure from former Socialist Prime Minister Zhan Videnov.

-- Bulgaria expects wheat output of 2.45 million tonnes from this year's harvest, but it could be lower after heavy rains and hailstorms in the second half of June hit the crop in the western parts of the country.
-- South Korea's Hyundai Corp bought last week a 70 percent share of Bulgaria's Elprom-Trapho electric parts producer for $2.9 million.
Hyundai had pledged to invest $4 million over the next five years in modernising the Sofia-based company, whose 1995 turnover was about $8.2 million.
-- The European Union has urged Bulgaria to amend its constitution to enable foreign citizens to buy local land, Foreign Minister Nadezhda Mihailova said.

-- Prince Kiril Saxe-Coburg-Gotha, son of Bulgaria's exiled King Simeon II and financial adviser to President Petar Stoyanov, is expected to visit Sofia this week. Kiril is an economist at London-based investment bank Lehman Brothers International which has shown interest in placing Bulgarian bonds on global markets.

-- Estonia, which has launched a currency board system five years ago, has offered to send its experts to to advise Bulgarian central bankers on the system's implementation, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said.

-- The Sofia City Court declared last week the private Slavyani Bank insolvent. The bank was placed in receivership on September 23 and the central bank filed an insolvency suit against it on October 31.
-- Bulgaria could receive some $800 million under World Bank investment projects if the government keeps the pace of the reforms, World Bank resident in Sofia Alberto Musalem said.
